doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: Kenny Davern pulls her on stage at the Clearwater festival
summary: Playing with Diva Jazz Orchestra, she was told to fetch her clarinet and Kenny Davern placed her between himself and Buddy DeFranco.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: That particular moment with the vibrato for some reason made me think of Kenny Davern. You had that particular tone and he’s been a favorite of mine and so I now have another favorite with you.

I loved Kenny Davern you know. It’s kind of — he was important in my path. Because years ago I played with, I played for many years with the Diva Jazz Orchestra, an all- female big band that exists for over 25 years. And we played the Clearwater Jazz Festival, it was around the year 2000. And it was Flip Phillips’ 85th birthday and at the end of the festival in the hotel everybody played “Happy Birthday” to Flip Phillips on stage, a bunch of musicians, including Buddy DeFranco and Kenny Davern. And Stanley Kay, the manager of Diva asked me, “Where is your clarinet?” And I’m like, “It’s in the hotel room.” It didn’t even occur to me, I wasn’t even, I was still playing saxophone. He says, “Go get it.” So I went to my room and by the time I came back to the stage they were already playing rhythm changes and you know everybody took a couple of choruses and I just went on stage and I went to the clarinet and I went to the front and I played two choruses of rhythm changes and then the minute I finished I had two hands grab me by the shoulder and led me back and it was Kenny Davern who held me and took me back and put me right between him and Buddy DeFranco. And that was a really, really important moment for me because it was a moment of his saying all right girl, you’re with us, which was — it still took me a minute to become a clarinetist but it was a really memorable moment, important.
